issues.display_title: Issue #979: Performance MapThru Mode: Slow Map
issues.main_description_html:
Feedback

WhatsApp.Video.2026-09-09.at.3.46.03.PM.mp4

RESULT

video-979-editor.mp4

Root cause. Three separate causes on the reported panorama route (4,696 points, 5,164 Information records), each confirmed with an A/B probe:

  1. Preview, zoomed in on the route: every point was a DOM marker button (858 on screen at z17.2) repositioned with style writes every frame, and the label canvas's text work in the same frame forced a style recalc over all of them (label pass 56.7 ms, render 77.3 ms per frame).
  2. Editor Map tab: each mousemove over a room calls setHoveredFeatureId(id). The setter always wrote a new state object and InformationListSection subscribed to the whole store, so every move re-rendered all 5,164 rows (a 15-move drag across the building took 86.7 s).
  3. Editor 2D plan: pan redraws on every pointermove, and each redraw drew every pin as a path, two fills and a stroke, plus one stroke per pano link (~9.4k fill/stroke calls per redraw).

Fix.

  1. Hover setters return the current state when the value is unchanged; InformationListSection is memoised, selects with useShallow and builds its rows in a useMemo.
  2. Plain plan pins are stamped with drawImage from one cached sprite, in model order (shared-path batching hid the white end/junction pins); pano links share one path and one stroke; pins and segments off the canvas are skipped.
  3. Preview marker dots are painted on one overlay canvas; a mousemove proxy leaves the nearest dot to its real DOM button, so hover, click and the tooltip still work. The editor Map tab keeps its DOM markers.

Result. Headless GPU probe: preview z17.2 drag median / p90 83.4 / 250 → 16.7 / 33.4 ms, long tasks 73 → 13; editor Map tab 15-move drag 86.7 s → 8.1 s; plan fill + stroke calls per redraw ~9.4k → 22. Recording rig (Vulkan): preview drag median frame 114 → 13 ms; Map tab moves handled in 10 s while hovering the building 2 → 53; 2D pan 10.6 → 13.5 fps (a modest gain: sprites cut GPU work about 3× but add main-thread work per redraw). Not addressed: the editor Map tab still idles at ~5–8 fps on this project (~126k DOM elements, a list without virtualisation), and preview canvas dots are not tab-focusable. pnpm test 2324 passed, lint and tsc clean.

Files: src/components/editor/map-markers/MapObjectMarkers.tsx, src/components/editor/map-markers/__tests__/MapObjectMarkers.test.tsx, src/components/editor/map-markers/__tests__/dotCanvas.test.ts, src/components/editor/map-markers/dotCanvas.ts, src/components/editor/panel/InformationListSection.tsx, src/lib/floorplanEditor/editor/__tests__/drawBatch.test.ts, src/lib/floorplanEditor/editor/draw.ts, src/lib/floorplanEditor/editor/drawBatch.ts, src/store/__tests__/useMapStore-hoverNoop.test.ts, src/store/mapStore/editorSlice.ts

issues.display_title: Issue #992: perf(editor): Map tab slow on large panorama projects (all list rows + markers mounted, autosave per change)
issues.main_description_html:
Demo by Developer

video-992-editor.mp4

Assigned to: Ibnu Rizqia Ramadan — Developer

Follow-up to #979. On the reported panorama route (c201d5e3: 4,696 points and 5,164 Information records on one level) the editor Map tab is still slow after #979: the HUD reads ~4–15 fps while idle or dragging, and a map drag over open basemap takes ~300 ms per pointer move — the same before and after #979 (33 vs 30 moves in 10 s on the recording rig). #979 removed the Information list re-render on every hover; what is left is how much stays mounted, plus one store subscriber.

Where the time goes

Measured on the #979 branch (headless Chrome on the GPU, Tesla P4, dev server), Map tab of a scratch copy:

  • DOM: 126,277 elements and 20,232 buttons — consistent with 5,164 Information rows × 3 buttons (expand, Edit, Delete) plus ~4,700 marker buttons.
  • 15-move drag across the building, 8.1 s wall clock. Top self time: (program) 5,299 ms (native work outside JS), MapObjectMarkers reposition 644 ms, useWizardPersistence subscriber 148 ms + localStorage.setItem 112 ms, getBoundingClientRect 65 ms.

Root cause (checked in code)

  1. The Information list mounts every row. InformationListSection renders all rows, each with its expand / Edit / Delete buttons. Nothing is windowed, and no virtualization package is installed.
  2. The editor mounts every marker. MapObjectMarkers.tsx:300 — renderedItems = showUnlinked || siteScaleOnly ? items : viewportItems. The one-viewport buffer the preview uses is skipped in the editor on purpose (comment at :259: the editor's points are draggable), so all 4,696 markers stay mounted and are repositioned every frame.
  3. Local autosave serializes on every store change. useWizardPersistence.ts:129 subscribes to every useMapStore change and writes JSON.stringify(buildPersistedState(state, session)) to localStorage — no filter, no debounce — so every change, hover included, pays for serializing a canvasData with 4,696 points.

Scope

  • InformationListSection — mount only the rows in view (windowing). Search, expand, row hover → map highlight, Edit / Delete / Unlink and keyboard focus keep working. No new dependency without asking first.
  • MapObjectMarkers in the editor (showUnlinked) — cull markers outside the viewport buffer, or paint far-zoom dots on a canvas as the preview does since #979 (dotCanvas.ts), without breaking drag-to-move: a marker being dragged stays mounted, and unlinked markers keep their dimmed look.
  • useWizardPersistence — skip the write when nothing buildPersistedState reads has changed, and/or debounce it, making sure the last change still lands before the page unloads.

Acceptance criteria

  • Editor Map tab on the reported project: idle and pan clearly smoother than today on the recording rig (target ≥ 30 fps idle; a basemap drag keeps up with the pointer). Measure before/after starting from .playwright-mcp/demo/979-editor/scenario.mjs.
  • Mounted DOM on that Map tab drops well below today's 126k elements / 20k buttons.
  • Hovering a list row still highlights its object on the map, and search still finds rows that are out of view.
  • Dragging a point marker to move it still works, including one that starts near the edge of the view.
  • A store change that does not alter anything buildPersistedState persists does not write to localStorage; editing the plan still autosaves locally.
  • pnpm test, pnpm lint, tsc --noEmit green; before/after demo per the demo convention.

RESULT

Root cause (measured, not assumed)

On a scratch copy of the reported project the Map tab mounted 126,275 elements. In-page A/B on development (hide one thing, re-measure, restore):

  • Idle at ~13 fps came from how much was mounted, not from JS: the map rendered 0 frames/s while idle and the main thread was mostly free. Hiding the Information list alone, or the marker overlay alone, brought idle to 60 fps.
  • Basemap drag at ~13 fps came from backdrop-blur on the ~70 visible marker labels, re-blurred over the moving map every frame. Turning that blur off in-page: 11 → 31 fps. Hiding the markers with display:none read as "no gain", but that variant was confounded (a 0 px size is never cached, so it forced layout every frame).
  • Local autosave serialized the whole project (~3.3 MB) on every store write, hover included.

Fix

  1. edebf7f perf(editor): skip the local autosave when nothing it persists changed — persistedStateChanged(state, prev) compares the fields buildPersistedState reads by reference; a test spies on buildPersistedState and fails if it reads a field the list misses.
  2. b955d10 perf(editor): mount the Information list a page at a time — 100 rows, then the next 100 when the list end scrolls into view (IntersectionObserver sentinel). Search still filters every record. No new dependency.
  3. c477bc5 perf(map): cull editor markers to the viewport, drop label blur while moving — the preview's one-viewport buffer now applies in the editor too, keyed by marker id (a kept item object would draw a moved point at its old position), and the marker being dragged is always kept. The overlay sets data-moving between movestart and moveend; label plates drop backdrop-blur for that time and look the same at rest.
  4. 3868e8d perf(map): render each object marker as its own memoised button — the buffer shifting after a pan rebuilt all ~1,100 buttons (690 ms render in the 2 s after release); now only markers that entered the buffer mount.
  5. 904d934 fix(map): stop a point marker's image from hijacking its drag — pre-existing since #276, found while checking the drag criterion: same on development. A press on the pin's <img> chip plus 1–2 px of movement started the browser's native image drag (dragstart@img → pointercancel → lostpointercapture), so the pin stopped following and the drop never landed. The draggable button now prevents dragstart.

Numbers

Headless Chrome on the GPU (Tesla P4, ANGLE GL ES), dev servers, same probe and same scratch copy, development c2b54ab (:6060) vs this branch (:6066):

Editor Map tab development this branch
DOM elements / buttons 126,275 / 20,232 9,836 / 1,427
Marker buttons mounted 4,714 1,101
Information rows mounted 5,166 102
Idle frame rate 13.2 fps 60.1 fps
Basemap drag, 10 s 13.6 fps, 55 moves 32.9 fps, 104 moves
Hover across the building, 10 s 122 moves 152 moves
localStorage writes while hovering 1 (3.3 MB) 0
Longest task after releasing a drag 0 ms 199 ms

Recording rig (real Chrome on X11, ANGLE Vulkan, Tesla P4), from the before/after demo:

development this branch
DOM elements / buttons 126,279 / 20,232 9,840 / 1,427
Idle, 5 s 21.6 fps 68.5 fps
Basemap drag, 8 s 10.7 fps, 23 moves 78 fps, 60 moves
Hover across the building, 10 s 169 moves 176 moves

(Xvfb does not cap rAF at 60 Hz, hence > 60 fps.)

Acceptance criteria

  • Idle ≥ 30 fps (60.1); a basemap drag handles about twice the pointer moves (55 → 104 in 10 s).
  • Mounted DOM well below 126k / 20k (9,836 / 1,427).
  • Hovering a list row still highlights its objects; search finds rows that are not mounted (unit tests).
  • Dragging a point marker works, including near the edge of the view: in the browser a pin 820 px from the edge dragged by (60, 40) and one 31 px from the edge dragged by (−90, −50) both landed exactly there, kept pointer capture, stayed mounted and autosaved the edit. It did not work on development either (fixed in 904d934, see above).
  • A store change that persists nothing does not write localStorage; a plan edit still does (unit tests; 0 writes while hovering in the browser).
  • pnpm test 246 files / 2,334 passed, pnpm lint, tsc --noEmit green; before/after demo .playwright-mcp/demo/992-editor/video-992-editor.mp4.

Trade-off and not addressed

  • Settle after a pan: markers entering the viewport buffer mount when the camera stops: longest task 199 ms in the dev build (development has none, it keeps all 4,714 mounted).
  • Pano connection lines are drawn on every map frame in the editor Map tab and project every vertex (~1 s of JS per 4 s of drag in useFloorPlanLabels draw). Out of this task's scope; candidate follow-up.
  • Editor tab (not Map) sidebar object list still mounts all 4,701 rows (~52k elements on that tab).
  • The Information list only grows as you scroll; scrolling thousands of rows deep mounts them (real windowing if that bites).

Files: src/lib/persistence/wizardState.ts, src/hooks/useWizardPersistence.ts, src/components/editor/panel/InformationListSection.tsx, src/components/editor/map-markers/MapObjectMarkers.tsx, plus tests wizardState.autosave.test.ts, InformationListSection.window.test.tsx, MapObjectMarkers.test.tsx. Probes: .playwright-mcp/demo/lag-followup/probe-992*.mjs.

PR: #993 (→ development)

issues.display_title: Issue #995: perf(editor): paint the Map tab's far-zoom marker dots on a canvas (connection lines ruled out)
issues.main_description_html:
Demo by Developer

video-995-editor.mp4

Assigned to: Ibnu Rizqia Ramadan — Developer

Re-scoped 2026-09-14 — measured: the connection lines are not the cost

Measured on a scratch copy of the reported project (development 946145e, headless Chrome on the GPU, basemap drag on the editor Map tab):

  • Connection lines ruled out. A line-level CPU profile of useFloorPlanLabels draw put the connection-line loop at ~10–15 ms per 4 s of drag. The hot line was ctx.font = "600 11px …": 257 ms at the landing camera, 1,851 ms zoomed out 3 levels. Chromium flushes pending style on every canvas font set, so that line pays for the DOM markers restyled earlier in the same frame. Chunk-culling the lines would save ~15 ms.
  • Zoomed out, the editor draws the route as thousands of DOM dots. Drag there: 3.6 fps. MapObjectMarkers reposition took 769–994 ms per 4 s; the screenshot shows the route as overlapping DOM dots. In-page A/B: skipping repeated font sets, or reading the canvas size without a layout read, only moves zoomed-out drag 3.7 → 4.7 / 4.6 fps, and the font guard merely moves the recalc into the frame lifecycle ((program) 611 → 3,634 ms).

New scope

  • In the editor Map tab, paint far-zoom (below DOT_ZOOM) marker dots on one canvas, as the preview has since #979 (dotCanvas.ts). The dot under the pointer keeps its real button, so click, the hover title and drag-to-move keep working. Hidden pins stay dimmed; unlinked markers stay red.
  • Read the map canvas size in reposition without a layout read, if repeated measurement shows it helps.

Acceptance criteria (replace the connection-line ones below)

  • Zoomed out on the reported project, a basemap drag is clearly faster than today's ~3.6 fps; the landing camera is no worse.
  • A far-zoom dot can still be clicked to select, shows its title on hover, and can be dragged to move (including near the edge of the view).
  • Hidden pins are dimmed and unlinked markers red on the canvas, as the DOM dots are today.
  • pnpm test, pnpm lint, tsc --noEmit green; before/after demo per the demo convention.

Original description (superseded by the re-scope above)

Follow-up to #992. After #992 the editor Map tab of the reported panorama route (4,696 points) idles at 60 fps and pans at ~33 fps (headless GPU probe), but the top JS cost of every map frame is now the pano connection lines: draw in src/lib/map/useFloorPlanLabels.ts took 973–1,047 ms of self time per 4 s of basemap drag (dev build, ~16–29 map frames/s).

Where the time goes (checked in code)

  • The editor Map tab always passes the connections: Editor3DMapView.tsx:226 resolvePanoConnections(...) ("shown always on the editor Map view"). Preview/live draw the same way when connections are on (PreviewOverlay.tsx:913).
  • useFloorPlanLabels already converts to Mercator and chains the links into polylines once per connection set (#976, connRef), but on every map render draw walks every vertex of every polyline: projScreen (4×4 multiply + divide) per vertex, then one lineTo per vertex that moved ≥ 1 px, then one stroke() (useFloorPlanLabels.ts:354–388). Nothing is culled to the viewport and nothing is reused between frames.
  • In Editor mode the rest of draw is light (only the hovered area's label, plus safety markers), so on this project the per-frame bulk is the connection lines. Confirm the split with a profile before changing anything.

Scope

  • Make the per-frame cost of the connection lines scale with what is on screen, not with the size of the route. Options to evaluate (pick by measurement):
    • cull whole polylines / chunks by a precomputed bounding box against the viewport before projecting any vertex;
    • precompute simplified polylines per zoom band (the #976 sub-pixel skip happens after projecting — decide before projecting);
    • draw them as a MapLibre line layer instead, if the floor-height requirement (lines lifted to the level's base height on a pitched camera) can still be met.
  • Keep the look and behaviour: same colour/width, drawn under the route line at floor height, correct under pitch/rotation, the #976 no-massing Overview behaviour, and the preview's connection toggle (#279/#544).
  • No new dependency without asking.

Acceptance criteria

  • On the reported project (scratch copy), the connection-line part of draw per 4 s basemap drag drops well below today's ~1 s (profile before/after with .playwright-mcp/demo/lag-followup/probe-992.mjs --profile), and the drag frame rate does not get worse.
  • Lines look the same as today at a zoomed-in, a zoomed-out and a pitched/rotated camera (screenshot comparison on the same pinned camera).
  • Preview with connections on and the #976 no-massing Overview still draw the lines.
  • pnpm test, pnpm lint, tsc --noEmit green; before/after demo per the demo convention.

RESULT

What the measurements showed

On a scratch copy of the reported project (development 946145e, headless Chrome on the GPU, basemap drag on the editor Map tab):

  • The connection lines were not the cost. A line-level CPU profile of useFloorPlanLabels draw put the connection-line loop at ~10–15 ms per 4 s of drag. The hot line was ctx.font = … (257 ms landing, 1,851 ms zoomed out): Chromium flushes pending style on every canvas font set, and that flush paid for the markers restyled earlier in the frame. Chunk-culling the lines would have saved ~15 ms, so it was not built.
  • Zoomed out, the editor drew the route as thousands of DOM dots and a drag ran at 3.6 fps, with MapObjectMarkers reposition at 769–994 ms per 4 s.
  • In-page A/B, three runs: skipping repeated font sets only moved the recalc into the frame lifecycle ((program) roughly doubled), so it was dropped. Reading the canvas size without a layout read cut reposition self time every run (landing ~100–130 ms, zoomed out ~280–550 ms per 4 s), so it was kept.

Fix

b2121a7 perf(map): paint the editor's far-zoom marker dots on a canvas

  • MapObjectMarkers: the far-zoom canvas dots the preview has used since #979 are now used in the editor too. The dot under the pointer is still its real button, so click, the hover title and drag-to-move go through it. A hidden pin keeps its dimmed look (the button's opacity is read with its colour).
  • dotCanvas.ts: dots carry an optional alpha; fills and rings are grouped by colour and opacity.
  • reposition reads the map canvas size once and on resize instead of clientWidth/clientHeight on every frame.

98483af fix(map): drop a dragged far-zoom dot where it was released

  • Pre-existing (same code on development), found while checking the drag criterion in the browser: a far-zoom dot moved by (60, 40) landed at (73, 40). The drag's grab offset used the label's data-ah (16–18 px) while reposition places a dot's button with a 5 px half-width, so every dot drop landed 11–13 px right of the pointer. The grab offset now uses the same half-width.

Numbers

Headless GPU probe, same scratch copy and cameras, before → after:

Editor Map tab, basemap drag before after
Zoomed out 3 levels (whole route as dots) 3.6 fps, 10 moves 13 fps, 27 moves
draw self time per 4 s (zoomed out) 2,182 ms 625 ms
Landing camera (labels, not dots) 20.1 fps, 34 moves 18.5 fps, 30 moves (within run-to-run noise)

Screenshots at pinned cameras, SSIM before vs after: landing 0.999997, pitched 0.9989, zoomed out 0.9937 (canvas vs DOM dot antialiasing in the dense route).

Recording rig: real Chrome on X11, ANGLE Vulkan, Tesla P4, Map tab zoomed out 3 levels — idle 20.8 → 78.8 fps (Xvfb does not cap rAF at 60 Hz); basemap drag 6.4 → 10.4 fps, 15 → 27 pointer moves in 8 s.

Acceptance criteria (re-scoped)

  • Zoomed out, a basemap drag is clearly faster (3.6 → 13 fps); the landing camera is no worse beyond noise.
  • A far-zoom dot can be clicked to select, shows its title on hover, and can be dragged to move, including near the edge: in the browser, hovering a painted dot brings up its real button; a dot 501 px from the edge dragged by (60, 40) and one 18 px from the edge dragged by (−90, 50) both landed exactly there (after 98483af; before it they landed 13 px right), kept pointer capture and autosaved; clicking a dot selected it.
  • Hidden pins dimmed and unlinked markers red on the canvas: colour and opacity come from the marker button itself (unit test for the dimmed paint).
  • pnpm test 246 files / 2,337 passed, pnpm lint, tsc --noEmit green; demo .playwright-mcp/demo/995/video-995-editor.mp4.

Not addressed

  • Zoomed out, markers still re-render when the viewport buffer shifts after a pan (the #992 settle), and the style recalc of the mounted marker buttons remains; 13 fps is better, not smooth.
  • The ctx.font flush in draw stays: guarding it only moved the work.
  • MapWallVertexHandles still reads clientWidth per frame (wall edit mode only).

PR: #998 (→ development)

issues.display_title: Issue #997: Fix Issue Mouse Hover does not Match the Selected Item
issues.main_description_html:
Feedback

WhatsApp.Video.2026-09-14.at.10.07.19.AM.mp4

Sample Test

https://map-thru.com/v/UkZnTKwv

RESULT

video-997-roof-logo-hit-box.mp4

Root cause. A Closed room's roof logo is laid out in a fixed FIT_BASE box — 512 px wide (height from the room's plan aspect) — and projected onto the roof by a transform on its <img>. A transform moves pixels, not layout, so the <button pointer-events:auto> around it kept the whole 512 px box. At mall zoom every roof logo carried an invisible rectangle many times the size of its room, lying over the neighbouring shops and taking their hovers and clicks. On /v/UkZnTKwv: cursor on Armani Exchange → Gap; cursor on Old Navy → Laser Clinics Canada (both in the recording). It also explains most of "wherever I click I get a store card".

Fix. Marker button is pointer-events: none when it holds a roof logo; the transformed <img> and the far-zoom dot take the pointer. Hit testing follows the transform, so a logo is hit where it is painted; events still bubble to the button (hover/click/title/focus unchanged). Same component in /v, /embed, preview and the editor Map tab.

Measured (GPU, recording's camera, 924 points on the live floor):

before after
pointer on another shop's logo box 59.3% 0%
highlight ≠ shop drawn under the pointer 59.3% 0%
same view screenshot SSIM 1.000 (nothing drawn moved)

Files. src/components/editor/map-markers/MapObjectMarkers.tsx, src/components/editor/map-markers/__tests__/MapObjectMarkers.test.tsx (+1 test). pnpm test 246 files · 2338 passed, lint 0 errors, tsc clean.

Demo. .playwright-mcp/demo/997/video-997-roof-logo-hit-box.mp4 — development vs fix, same camera: Old Navy → Laser Clinics Canada → Old Navy; Simons → Sport Chek → Simons (asserted in the scenario).

Not covered. Clicking a shop still flies to it and opens its card (by design). A drag that starts on a label pill still does not pan/rotate the map. "Directions unclear" needs its own task.

issues.display_title: Issue #996: perf(editor): Editor tab object list mounts every row on large panorama projects
issues.main_description_html:
Demo by Developer

video-996-editor.mp4

Assigned to: Ibnu Rizqia Ramadan — Developer

Follow-up to #992, which fixed the same pattern on the Map tab. The Editor tab's sidebar object list still mounts one row per object: on the reported panorama route (4,701 objects on one floor) the Editor tab measured 52,071 elements and 4,729 buttons, 4,699 of them the per-row layer-order menu triggers (headless GPU probe, development c2b54ab, scratch copy). Frame-rate impact on the Editor tab has not been measured yet.

Where the cost is (checked in code)

  1. Every row is mounted. UnifiedObjectList (src/components/editor/panel/UnifiedObjectList.tsx:107) maps all rows inline, no paging and no per-row memo.
  2. Each row carries its own menu component. Every reorderable row renders LayerOrderMenu (LayerOrderMenu.tsx), which on its own calls useFloorplanEditorStore, useEditorCapabilities, useContext and useState and mounts a Popover trigger button — about 4.7k of each on this project.
  3. The whole list re-renders on any selection. UnifiedObjectList subscribes to eight selection slices of useFloorplanEditorStore (walls, doors, windows, rooms, manual area, rooms list, annotation, shape), so selecting anything re-renders every row; isSelected for an Area does rooms.find per row.
  4. ObjectSection re-renders on every map store write. ObjectSection.tsx:31 calls useMapStore() with no selector.
  5. Quadratic pano lookup. hasPanoInfo (ObjectSection.tsx:42) does informationRecords.find per object, so each rebuild of objects is ~4.7k × 5.2k comparisons — the same pattern #979 removed from InformationListSection.

Scope

  • Measure first: on a scratch copy, the Editor tab's idle frame rate, a 2D pan, and a canvas selection, with the list present vs hidden in-page (the #992 A/B method, .playwright-mcp/demo/lag-followup/probe-992-isolate.mjs), so the fix is sized to what actually costs.
  • Mount the All list a page at a time as it scrolls (as InformationListSection does since #992, IntersectionObserver, no new dependency), and check whether the per-type lists (EngineWallList, EngineRoomList, EngineOpeningList, SimpleAnnotationList, AccessList) need the same.
  • Render rows through a memoised row component so a selection change only re-renders the rows whose selected state changed; resolve per-row lookups (rooms.find, pano info) through maps built once.
  • Select only the fields ObjectSection reads from useMapStore (useShallow).
  • Keep behaviour: filters and counts, search over every object (not only mounted rows), row click / Shift / Ctrl-Cmd selection, hover-to-locate on the canvas, the layer-order menu and its reset to All (#945/#949), viewer read-only rows (§B7). No new dependency without asking.

Acceptance criteria

  • Before/after numbers for the Editor tab on the reported project (scratch copy): mounted elements/buttons drop well below 52k / 4.7k, and idle / pan / select are no worse (better where the A/B showed the list costs).
  • Search finds an object whose row is not mounted; filter counts are unchanged.
  • Selecting on the canvas still highlights the row; hovering a row still locates its object; the layer-order menu still reorders and resets the filter to All.
  • A viewer still sees read-only rows with no menu.
  • pnpm test, pnpm lint, tsc --noEmit green; before/after demo per the demo convention.

RESULT

What the measurements showed

On a scratch copy of the reported project (development 380f791, headless Chrome on the GPU, Editor tab, 4,701 objects on the floor):

  • Mounted DOM: 52,070 elements, 4,729 buttons — 4,701 object rows, 4,696 of them with their own layer-order menu.
  • Selecting a point froze the page ~7 s (median 6.6–7.1 s from selectAnnotationAt to the next painted frame; the engine's own work was 59–79 ms). A CPU profile of two selections put the render on UnifiedObjectList re-rendering every row — its rows map 1,161 ms inclusive, LayerOrderMenu 931 ms of that (Popover tree, capabilities hook) — plus dev-build React element churn and GC. ObjectSection did not appear: a selection only writes the editor store.
  • Not list-bound: idle (53–54 fps) and the 2D pan (~20 fps) measured the same with the list's scroller hidden in-page.

Fix

5a9aacb perf(editor): page the object list and memoise its rows

  • UnifiedObjectList mounts 100 rows at a time and adds the next page when the end of the list scrolls into view (IntersectionObserver, no new dependency), like the Information list since #992. An edit that rebuilds the rows keeps what is mounted; ObjectSection keys the list by filter and search, so a new query starts from the first page.
  • Rows are a memoised ObjectRow, so a selection re-renders only the rows whose selected state changed.
  • ObjectSection selects only the five map-store fields it reads (useShallow) and resolves pano-linked Information through a Set built once instead of a find per object.

c97c690 perf(editor): page the per-type object lists too

  • Checking the per-type lists (task scope) found the same problem in SimpleAnnotationList (Points, Safety, Shapes, Panoramas): every filtered row mounted with its own layer-order menu and delete button, all re-rendered on each selection, a whole-store subscription, rows re-derived on every render — the Panoramas arm with an informationRecords.find per object, twice.
  • Same paging and memoised row (carrying the delete-confirm state); useShallow; rows derived and filtered in useMemo; deriveAnnotationRows indexes the records by id once.

Numbers

Headless GPU probe, same scratch copy, before → after:

Editor tab, All list before after
DOM elements / buttons 52,070 / 4,729 1,461 / 133
Object rows / layer-order menus mounted 4,701 / 4,696 100 / 100
Selecting a point, median to the painted frame 7,135 ms 260 ms
Idle 53 fps 59 fps
2D pan (not list-bound) ~15–20 fps ~14–21 fps

issues.display_title: Issue #1004: Handle Issue Opening Hours Information does not Match the Device's Time
issues.main_description_html:
Feedback

WhatsApp.Video.2026-09-14.at.1.51.01.PM.mp4

RESULT

video-1004.mp4

Cause

Not a server or device clock bug. Open/closed on the visitor card follows the building's local time, resolved in the browser from the project pin — PRD #473 decision 12.8, implemented in #494. The server's clock is never used.

The reported project is pinned in Toronto (the wizard's default pin). The video was recorded around Monday 13:50 WIB, which is Monday 02:50 in Toronto, so every status in it is right for the building:

Object Monday hours Card At 02:50 in Toronto
rectangle Open 24 hours Open now ✅
triangle 09:00–17:00 Closed ✅
circle 18:00–23:00 Closed ✅

The card never said which clock it used, so on a laptop in Jakarta (where the triangle should be open at 13:50) it read as wrong. Note: the PRD's visitor-hours section still says status "uses the saved hours and the visitor's device time"; decision 12.8 and the Key Decisions in #473 supersede it.

Fix

63e81e6 fix(preview): name the building's local time on the Hours status — PR #1005

  • buildingTimeLabel(location, now) in src/lib/hours.ts names the building's wall clock, e.g. Mon, 02:50 Eastern Time, or returns null when the project has no pin or the device already reads the same time.
  • The collapsed Hours row of PreviewInfoCard shows Local time Mon, 02:50 Eastern Time under the status when the label is set. A visitor already on the building's clock sees no change.

Verification

  • The reporter's project in /preview (read-only), Chrome at 14:30 WIB:
    • this branch, browser timezone Asia/Jakarta: all three cards show Local time Mon, 03:30 Eastern Time under Open now / Closed / Closed;
    • this branch, browser timezone America/Toronto: no extra line;
    • development, Asia/Jakarta: Closed with no line (the report).
  • Unit tests: buildingTimeLabel (another timezone → label; same timezone or no pin → null) and the card (label under the status for a visitor elsewhere, nothing for a visitor on the building's clock).

Not addressed

issues.display_title: Issue #1007: perf(editor): Editor tab 3D pane renders ~40k draw calls every frame on large floor plans
issues.main_description_html:
Assigned to: Ibnu Rizqia Ramadan — Developer

Reported with a screen recording (samples/editor-super-lag.mp4, 2026-09-14): on Square One Mall V6 (Demo), Level 2, the editor's Map tab holds 60 fps, but switching to the Editor tab drops the page to 9-12 fps and it stays there while panning and zooming the 2D plan.

Measured (headless GPU probe, development 5f3e837, scratch copy of the project, Level 2)

Level 2 has 4,258 walls, 6 doors, 276 rooms, 45 manual areas, 18 access markers. The Editor tab's side 3D pane builds 9,595 meshes = 39,649 draw calls, 381k triangles per frame. In-page A/B with the engine's own pause flag (setPaused), no code change, each state measured twice:

3D pane rendering 3D pane paused
idle frame rate 4.5 fps 60 fps
2D plan pan (one pointermove per frame) 2.0-2.9 fps 6.5-13.6 fps

Probe: .playwright-mcp/demo/lag-followup/probe-editor-2d3d.mjs.

Where the cost is (checked in code)

  1. The 3D pane renders every animation frame, forever. The engine loop (src/lib/floorplanEditor/editor/index.ts:110) calls scene.step() → controls.update(); renderer.render(scene, camera) on every rAF whether or not anything changed. The 2D plan and the 3D pane share the main thread and the GPU, so an idle or 2D-only interaction pays a full three.js render of ~40k draw calls each frame. (The CPU profile with the pane on is all three.js: setup, needsUpdate, renderBufferDirect, projectObject, painterSortStable.)
  2. The 2D redraw recomputes geometry that a pan does not change. With the pane paused, the pan profile's top app costs per redraw are:
    • logoFitBox → pointInPolygon for every Closed room with a logo (draw.ts:254): ~400 ms per 6 s pan;
    • devicePixelRatio read on every px() call (view.ts), thousands per redraw: ~370 ms;
    • wallOpenings twice per wall against all doors and all windows (draw.ts:219-221), including the empty window list: ~160 ms.

Scope

  • Render the 3D pane on demand: only when the camera moved (OrbitControls.update() returns true, damping included), the scene was rebuilt or recoloured, the theme or size changed, or an async logo texture landed. Keep the loop and the setPaused flag as they are.
  • In the 2D redraw, stop recomputing pan-invariant geometry: cache the logo fit box per room geometry, read devicePixelRatio once per redraw instead of per px(), and skip wallOpenings for an empty opening list.
  • Out of scope: merging the 3D wall/joint meshes into fewer draw calls (only orbiting the 3D pane itself would still be slow); a rAF throttle for 2D pan redraws.
  • Frontend only, no Go API contract change, no new dependency.

Acceptance criteria

  • On the reported project (scratch copy), Editor tab idle frame rate with the pane rendering is ~60 fps (was 4.5), and the 2D pan is at least as fast as the "3D paused" baseline above.
  • The 3D pane still follows every change: orbit/pan/zoom including damping, wall/room edits, hover highlight from the 2D plan and from the pane, theme switch, resize, Closed-room logos that load after the build, returning from the Map tab.
  • The 2D plan draws exactly as before: logos and names in the same place, openings cut into walls, handles at the same size on HiDPI.
  • pnpm test, pnpm lint, tsc --noEmit green; before/after measurement per the demo convention.

RESULT

Root cause. The editor engine's rAF loop rendered the three.js pane on every animation frame whether or not anything had changed. Level 2 of the reported mall (4,258 walls) is 9,595 meshes = 39,649 draw calls per frame, on the same main thread and GPU as the 2D plan: the Editor tab idled at 4.5 fps and every 2D pan redraw paid a full 3D render too.

Fix.

  1. scene3d.ts: the pane renders on demand. A dirty flag is set by the controls' change event (pointer, wheel, damping), build, a logo texture landing, recolor, applyTheme, resizeRenderer and webglcontextrestored; step() renders only when dirty. The loop and setPaused are unchanged.
  2. draw.ts / closedRoom.ts: the 2D redraw stops recomputing what a pan cannot change: cachedLogoFitBox keyed by the room ring and checked against its coordinates (an Area drag moves vertices in place), line widths and handle radii once per redraw, one straight stroke for a wall with no opening.
  3. geometry.ts openingReach / mayCarryOpening: a wall whose box misses every opening's box grown by the match tolerance skips doorSpanOnWall, which had become the pan's top cost after (1).

Result. Headless GPU (Tesla P4), scratch copy of the reported project, Level 2, development vs this branch alternated twice, 3D pane rendering:

development this branch
idle 3.9–5.1 fps 60 fps
2D pan, first measured pass 2.1–2.3 fps 4.9–7.1 fps
2D pan, warm pass 3.3–3.4 fps 15.8–21.8 fps
3D renders during a 5 s pan one per 2D redraw 0

The pane still follows every change (three's render counter + screenshots): idle 2 s → 0 renders; an orbit drag renders and stops after damping; hover recolour, resize and Map tab → back each repaint, never blank. Pan fps rises run to run on both builds (JIT warm-up), so the table compares the same pass.

Not addressed: orbiting the 3D pane itself still renders ~40k draw calls per frame (merging/instancing the wall meshes is the follow-up if that matters); 2D pan redraws are still synchronous per pointermove.

Tests: scene3d-render-on-demand.test.ts (6, all fail on development's scene3d.ts), closedRoom.test.ts +3, opening-reach.test.ts (2; the property test fails without the tolerance growth). pnpm test 250 files / 2362 passed, pnpm lint and tsc --noEmit clean.
